headline: The hands are fixed and you can see it in the game: the same NPC, the same camera, the same GPU, one file different — an egg with three stubs becomes four clawed digits with the room visible between them, and 52 of 60 hand close-ups differ between the arms by a median 5.6-7.2% of the whole frame. The feet are NOT fixed and the evidence is the cleanest number in the pack: on the player's foot close-ups, NOT ONE PIXEL differs between the arms, on frames whose luma span is 156-176. And 148 of 408 NPCs have no face at all — the humanoid head is a bald ovoid with no eyes, nose, mouth, ears, brow or jaw, from all four bearings.

the_judgement_in_one_line_each.hands: YES, BETTER, AND VISIBLY SO. 52 of 60 hand close-ups differ, median 5.6-7.2% of frame, max 55.9%; C4 differs on 40 of 40. Still wrong: the digits are near-constant-thickness sausages and the claws are nearly as long as the segments carrying them, so from below the hand reads as a raptor's foot or a gripper. It is a hand now; it is not yet a good hand.
the_judgement_in_one_line_each.feet: NO. NOT ONE PIXEL DIFFERS on the player's foot close-ups — 3 of 3 static F1 frames byte-identical, 7 of 8 walking foot frames byte-identical, the eighth at 0.053%, all LIVE with luma span 156-176. The legs end in flat-bottomed trouser cylinders. The heel, sole, ball and three clawed toes round 4 built are not on screen. HYPOTHESIS for the next builder, not a finding: the leg clothing volume is a solid tapered tube whose rim sits at or below the ankle and the foot is built inside it — the same defect class as r4's own headline, one joint further down.
the_judgement_in_one_line_each.faces: SPLIT, AND THE HUMAN HALF IS THE WORST THING IN THESE FRAMES. Reptilian heads have a snout, two yellow eyes, a nostril and a crest, and read at conversation distance. Humanoid heads are bald ovoids: no eyes, no nose, no mouth, no ears, no brow, no jaw, no hair, from all four bearings. COUNTED THIS TURN from `game/data/npcs/*.json` (18 files, 408 records with a race): reptilian 260, humanoid 148. So 148 of 408 = 36.3% of the cast has no face, and the 6 khajiit in that 148 get a human egg, which is its own gap.
the_judgement_in_one_line_each.walk: NOT A RIGID GLIDE, BUT A STIFF SHUFFLE. Leg-band silhouette XOR 27.777 px against head-band 7.807 (ratio 3.56) versus a stick-at-zero null of 2.767 / 1.441 (ratio 1.92) — there is a leg cycle above the noise. What is missing is the two loudest cues: no heel strike and no toe-off, because there is no foot. The before and after arms agree to within 0.03 px on every band, which is the correct null — round 4 changed no animation.
the_judgement_in_one_line_each.r4_open_regression: NOT VISIBLE. The daylight `actor-orbit-holes.mjs` counts is the room showing BETWEEN THE DIGITS, which is the point of the round and exactly the 'legitimate through-gap' r4 guessed the depth heuristic could not distinguish. On the ankle hypothesis the evidence is unusually clean: the player is saxhleel, the same body whose `cloth/calf_l` tally moved 8,881 -> 61,788 offline, and its foot frames are BYTE-IDENTICAL between the arms. A seam worth 53,000 border pixels offline produces zero changed pixels in a live frame pointed at that ankle. That does not prove the offline number wrong; it proves the regression is not visible, which is what I was asked.
the_judgement_in_one_line_each.overall: No, the characters do not look good. The figures read as slabs — a broad flat-fronted torso, legs merging into one column at most bearings, no deltoid, one uninflected colour per surface, a neck nearly as wide as the skull. Round 4 fixed the hands, and the hands were never the first thing you look at.

what_i_found_in_the_tooling.id: 1. `setInput` IS NOT A HARNESS VERB, so no capture in this project has ever photographed a moving player
what_i_found_in_the_tooling.evidence: `grep -rn setInput game/` -> 0 matches. `f10-r3-materials.mjs:341` and `f10-r4-digits.mjs:267` both open their motion block with `await call('setInput', { forward: 1 })`; `call()` turns a missing method into `{ok:false}` and neither tool checks it. The frames still differ from each other because water and foliage move, so nothing looked wrong.
what_i_found_in_the_tooling.measured_not_eyeballed: Across r3's whole 'walk', the outer 6% border ring — pure background, since the camera tracks the body — changes on 185 of 91,904 pixels, 0.2%, first frame against last. The same measurement on this round's walk, same camera rule, same canvas: 65,576 of 91,904, 71.35%.
what_i_found_in_the_tooling.the_real_path: `queueInputs`: a `move` event sets moveX/moveY and THEY PERSIST until another event changes them (`game/src/input/pipeline.js:211-213`). This round queues one event per simulated frame and the player travelled 3.315 m over 64 frames with the stick at 0.55.

what_i_found_in_the_tooling.id: 2. THE LIVENESS GATE HAS BEEN CALLED WITH ARGUMENT NAMES IT DOES NOT HAVE

Neither key exists, so `box` was null and `subject` was false on EVERY frame either tool ever took — the 'is the thing I am measuring in it' half of HAZARDS 15 never ran, and `subject_box.from` would have said so in the manifest if anyone had read it.
what_i_found_in_the_tooling.fixed_here: 159 of 159 frames carry a projected box and a recorded verdict.

instruments_built.tools/visual/f10-r5-appearance.mjs: The capture. Region-scale framing for face/hand/foot from skeleton.json's own offset chain (head 1.6400, hand_l 0.9100, foot_l 0.0900, height_m 1.78, summed by script not retyped); each hand bearing shot to BOTH sides of the body axis along the camera's own right vector, because `listEntities()` reports no yaw and a hand's azimuth is unknown; `mustCall` for verbs whose failure must not be swallowed; motion via queueInputs with the player's position recorded every frame.
instruments_built.tools/visual/f10-r5-walk-silhouette.mjs: Per-row silhouette XOR banded head/torso/leg, with a walking-vs-frozen self-test, 5/5 green. ITS FIRST DESIGN WAS WRONG AND ITS OWN SELF-TEST REFUSED IT: counting off-background pixels per row scores a scissoring leg at exactly 0, because two bars moving apart keep the same pixel count. The statistic had to be sensitive to WHERE the mask is. The self-test's second failure was in the fixture, not the tool — the synthetic figure's feet touched the border ring, which is the background model, teaching the mask that the figure's own colour was background.
instruments_built.tools/visual/fixtures/f10-r5-control-act: b175da8e's actor.js, byte-identical, so a control arm can run on a Pod that has no `.git`.
